prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational. Asset type: a beautiful primary-school illustrated drawing reference sheet for an original Chinese folktale interactive story about Ma Liang's magic brush. Generate a brand new landscape image, approximately 1536x1024. No writing of any kind.

Composition: one unbroken warm ivory handmade paper background with three equally spacious independent miniature dioramas in a horizontal row; no boxes, no thick borders. Generous clean breathing room above and between objects. All three devices are equally prominent, detailed, physically plausible, easy for children to observe before drawing their own invention. Quiet decorative ground shadows, no characters. Isometric 3/4 perspective allowing the mechanism and water height difference to be seen.

LEFT THIRD: a traditional Chinese wooden bucket water-lifting wheel standing VERTICALLY in a low river, on a HORIZONTAL axle held by two strong timber A-frame posts. A big clearly visible spoked timber wheel with small scooping buckets around its rim; the bottom buckets dip below the water surface, the buckets rise up the side, and a bucket near the top visibly tips water into a separate HIGH wooden collection trough. This high trough carries the lifted water horizontally a short distance to a higher bank. Show an unmistakable small stream of water from top bucket into top trough. Clear wooden joints and fine timber grain, translucent jade water. This is a lifting wheel, not a flat horizontal wheel and not an undershot water-powered mill connected to grinding machinery.

MIDDLE THIRD: a simple irrigation bamboo aqueduct: several open split-bamboo trough pieces joined smoothly end-to-end, with no leaks, on diminishing-height wooden trestles. Clean side view with 3/4 depth. A SMALL raised spring pool at upper left feeds the highest bamboo trough. The bamboo channel visibly slopes continuously downward from left to right, with turquoise water running along its hollow center, and its low open outlet pours gently into furrows beside a small green vegetable bed at lower right. No wheel, no reservoir wall, no stairs in the channel, water never flows uphill. The source is clearly higher than the vegetables.

RIGHT THIRD: a low grey-stone rectangular storage reservoir filled with jade water; one front-facing outlet near the bottom is equipped with a plainly visible vertical sliding wooden sluice gate with two guide posts and a wooden lifting handle. Gate raised partway, a small turquoise stream emerges through the opening UNDER the gate into a low channel and then waters a tiny vegetable plot. Reservoir walls continuous and substantial, stored water visible inside below wall height, gate controls the only outflow. No wheel, no bamboo aqueduct. Distinguish the raised storage water level from the lower outflow channel.

Art direction: refined Chinese children's picture-book illustration; mineral malachite green and azurite blue, warm fine wood, pale ochre paper, restrained delicate antique-gold contour details, elegant multi-layer paper-sculpture depth and soft realistic cast shadows. Every miniature feels tactile and dimensional, not a flat icon. Sophisticated yet friendly, highly polished detailed educational art, clear structure rather than decorative clutter. Fine stone and wood texture, crisp edges. No photorealistic photography, no cartoon faces, no labels, letters, words, arrows, numerals, captions, watermark, UI, arrows, heavy borders. The three systems must remain completely separate.
referenceUse: Observed for art direction only; no copied composition or typography

inspection.wheel: Vertical wheel and horizontal axle; rim buckets shown lifting water from low river and discharging to high trough.
inspection.bamboo: Raised source visibly higher than vegetables; continuous downward bamboo trough on timber supports.
inspection.reservoir: Stone tank stores water, wooden sliding gate visibly controls low outflow to vegetable furrows.
inspection.text: No text, labels, numbers, watermark or UI.
